Subject: Dedicated vs hyperscaler: post-demo recap + POC next steps

Hi Daniel — thanks again for the time today. Quick recap from our discovery/demo and proposed next steps: 

Summary of what we heard:
- Primary goal: consistent low-latency inference for customer-facing chat at 99th percentile < 120ms.
- Current evaluation: testing on hyperscaler GPU pools (AWS/GCP) but hitting capacity variability during peak hours and concerns about unit cost at scale.
- Compliance: data residency in US-only region; procurement will require an SOW and capacity guarantees.

How Redwood Dedicated maps to your needs (high level):
- Reserved GPU pools with committed throughput and predictable latency SLOs.
- Routing/fallback: we can configure cross-region fallback or burst to hyperscaler if you want a hybrid safety net.
- Cost controls: batching, KV/prefix caching, and quantization profiles tuned for your workload to reduce per-token cost.

Proposed POC (short):
1) 2-week technical POC comparing: Redwood Dedicated (reserved) vs your hyperscaler baseline.
2) Test matrix: baseline latency (p50/p95/p99), sustained throughput, cold-start/scale behavior, and failover.
3) Success criteria: p99 < 120ms at 1.5x peak TPS and cost target in alignment with procurement.

Next steps / asks:
- Can you share a short capacity forecast (expected peak TPS and concurrency) and preferred model family/version? (attaching our capacity brief)
- Would procurement want a draft SOW before we schedule the kickoff?
- Availability for a 30-min kickoff next week (I propose Wed/Thu morning PT).

I've attached a short capacity brief and a proposed test matrix. Looping in Kimberly (sales) and Lauren (solutions) to scope and run the POC.

Thanks —
Markus
Senior Solutions, Redwood Inference

Markus — thanks for the summary and for the demo. That aligns with what we discussed internally. A few clarifications from our side:

- Our current peak is around 800 concurrent inference requests with spiky bursts up to ~1,400 for short windows. We expect 30% growth over the next 6 months.
- We're testing on AWS managed endpoints; the variability comes from noisy neighbor behavior and preemption during autoscale events.
- Procurement will want an explicit capacity guarantee and an agreed SLA for latency and availability.

I've attached our internal forecast (simple spreadsheet) to give you numbers for the POC. For the POC, we want to validate cost at 1.5x peak (so ~2,100 concurrent equivalent) and also the worst-case cold-start behavior.

We're open for Wed and Thu next week (UTC-7 mornings). Procurement asked if you can provide a draft SOW and an initial quote for a 6-month reserved capacity option to review with finance.

Thanks,

Hi all — looping in a POC plan draft below. I'm copying the plan into the thread and also sharing a Drive folder for artifacts.

POC objective: Validate Redwood Dedicated reserved capacity vs ACME hyperscaler baseline across latency, throughput, and operational behavior.

Test matrix (high level):
- Workloads: chat (short tokens ~25), completions (longer tokens ~150)
- Concurrency targets: steady 800, peak 1,400, burst test at 2,100 (1.5x peak)
- Metrics: p50/p95/p99 latency, tokens/sec, GPU utilization, cold-start time, failover latency (if we trigger fallback to hyperscaler)
- Duration: 10 business days of steady-state tests + 2 days of stress/failover tests

Technical prerequisites:
- Model: please confirm model family/version you want us to run (we recommend a quantized variant for Dedicated if you want better cost/perf).
- Access: a short list of test prompts (sanitized), a service account or temporary token to replay traffic, and firewall/IP allowlist for our POC cluster.
- Data residency: we'll run in a US-only VPC with encrypted at-rest storage; logs can be shared via the Drive folder.

Deliverables:
- Daily test reports (CSV + dashboards), final comparison deck, and a recommended configuration for production (batching, cache policies, quantization profile).

Drive folder: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2B3cRedwood-ACME-POC

I'll prepare the detailed test scripts (locust/jmeter) and the CSV template for the test results. Attaching the proposed CSV test matrix.

Thanks —
Lauren
